terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, transitive; of animals, people, fruit
evidence: Cato Agr. 64.1: oleam (cōgere), to gather (Lewis & Short)
Traupman p. 107: round up, cōgō, cōgere, coēgī, coāctum
terms.comment: From co-agō, “drive together”: the shepherd’s verb for bringing in the flock.

phrases.english: Let’s gather the dolls and balls.

sources: The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
Lewis & Short: cogo
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
